title: Articles / genericity
note: zero article + plural for general statements · zero article with uncountable nouns · `the` + adjective for a group, `the` + nationality, `the` with one-of-a-kind nouns · six generic/specific minimal pairs with the same noun · zero-article items gap the bare noun, so no item has an empty answer · 4 strands x 12 · 48 items · built to live 2026-08-07 (cloud run 9)

cards.title: Talking about things in general: leave the article out
cards.body: For a general statement English uses a plural noun or an uncountable noun with no article at all. Czech has no articles, so this is the one case where Czech and English agree — the trap is putting `the` in because the sentence feels definite.
cards.body_cz: Pro obecné tvrzení používá angličtina množné číslo nebo nepočitatelné jméno zcela bez členu. Čeština členy nemá, takže právě tady se obě řeči shodují — chybou je vložit `the` jen proto, že věta zní určitě.

The coffee in this shop is very good.

The children are in the garden.

cards.title: Uncountable nouns never take `a`
cards.body: These nouns have no plural and no `a`, even where Czech happily uses a plural.
cards.body_cz: Tato jména nemají množné číslo ani `a`, i když čeština množné číslo běžně používá.
points: information — not an information, not informations
news — looks plural, behaves singular: The news is good.
furniture · knowledge · patience · bread · petrol · traffic
money is singular: The money is in the bank.

cards.title: `the` + adjective = a group of people
cards.body: `the rich` means all rich people. The adjective takes no plural -s, and the verb is plural.
cards.body_cz: `the rich` znamená všichni bohatí. Přídavné jméno nemá koncovku -s a sloveso je v množném čísle.
points: the rich · the poor · the young · the old · the unemployed
The rich are — not The rich is, not The richs
Nationalities the same way: the French · the English · the Czechs
the Czechs takes -s; the French and the English do not

cards.title: `the` with things there is only one of
cards.title_cz: `the` u věcí, které jsou jen jedny
cards.body: If there is only one of something in the shared world, English marks it with `the`. Czech marks nothing, so this is the article Czech speakers drop most often.
cards.body_cz: Existuje-li něco jen jednou, angličtina to označí členem `the`. Čeština neoznačí nic, a proto Češi právě tento člen nejčastěji vynechávají.
points: the internet · the moon · the government · the police
the countryside · the city (as opposed to the countryside)
The police is a plural noun: The police have arrived.
